profile.bio: As a Doctoral Researcher at Sungkyunkwan University pursuing a Doctor of Science degree, I focus on advancing the field through innovative simulations and leveraging strong analytical skills. My academic foundation includes a Master’s Degree in Physics from Hanoi University of Science and Technology (2024). I collaborate on research initiatives aimed at addressing critical energy challenges, utilizing simulation tools to analyze complex systems. My work reflects a commitment to driving impactful solutions in semiconductor technologies while contributing to academic and scientific advancements.

papers.title: Universal hydrogen-free synthesis and elemental doping of two-dimensional transition metal selenides
papers.authors: Ping Man, Lok Wing Wong, Ka Ho Leung, Zhiqiang Guan, Tianren Chen, Honglin Chen et al.
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional transition metal selenides (TMSs) feature notable bandgap flexibility, versatile doping characteristics, and practical manufacturability, positioning them as promising candidates for next-generation electronics. However, their synthesis remains a critical bottleneck, as conventional chemical vapor deposition (CVD) routes require H2 assistance for selenization, raising safety, cost, and quality concerns and constraining elemental doping. Here we show a universal, H2-free CVD method that overcomes these limitations. Our approach produces a broad spectrum of 2D TMSs, including monolayer binaries, bilayer polytypes, alloys, and heterostructures, and is compatible with diverse substrates. Incorporating common metals (Al, Zn, Fe, Ni, Cu) into the precursor enhances growth kinetics and enables precise doping. Al-doped WSe2 exhibits markedly lower resistance, with centimeter-scale films attaining a hole mobility of 28.36 cm2 V−1 s−1 and an on/off ratio of 3.56×106, comparable to exfoliated and H2-assisted monolayers. This work establishes a safe, scalable, and tunable synthesis strategy for high-performance 2D electronics. 2D transition metal selenides (TMSs) exhibit interesting (opto-)electronic properties, but their bottom-up synthesis usually requires H2 gas, leading to safety concerns and cost implications. Here, the authors report a universal H2-free chemical vapour deposition method to grow large-scale metal-doped 2D TMSs on various substrates.

papers.title: What Is the Role of a Magnetic Mo Antisite Defect on Carrier Relaxation and Spin Dynamics in 2-D MoS<sub>2</sub>?
papers.authors: Chengan Lei, Zhao Qian, Yandong Ma, Rajeev Ahuja
papers.abstract: Antisite defects significantly influence the dynamic properties of monolayer MoS 2, yet the carrier relaxation and spin dynamics in spin-polarized Mo antisite-defective MoS 2 remain unclear. Understanding these processes is crucial for advancing optoelectronic, spintronic, and valleytronic devices. Here, we employ first-principles calculations and ab initio nonadiabatic molecular dynamics with spin–orbit coupling (SOC) to explore carrier relaxation and spin dynamics in MoS 2 with a Mo antisite defect. This defect alters the material’s magnetic properties, leading to distinct relaxation behaviors: electron relaxation is slower than hole relaxation, and charge carriers in different spin channels exhibit varied dynamics. These differences arise from variations in electron–phonon coupling, SOC strength, and phonon mode activation. Our findings provide key insights into charge and spin dynamics in MoS 2 with magnetic defects and suggest strategies to enhance the performance of next-generation optoelectronic, spintronic, and valleytronic devices.
